title: Control Plane Evidence Graph
assertions: every evidence chain must connect observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next loop
change and verifier refs must point to existing repository files or package directories
artifact evidence refs are names only and must stay redacted
evidence graph records explain why a loop exists without relying on narrative memory
frontend handoff decisions that change thread semantics must connect to the closed-loop claim that enforces them
cross-repository lifecycle observations must become owned open questions when this repository cannot safely change the runtime owner
evidence graph evidence must publish generated_at and expires_at and refresh on a schedule
evidence graph refresh evidence must expose workflow_file, cadence_minutes, and manual_refresh_command, and the workflow must upload the evidence artifact with strict if-no-files-found behavior
every evidence graph chain must cite at least one Loop Registry claim so reasoning routes cannot become orphan narrative records

chains.observation: Provider, smoke, load, performance, and release-readiness harness failures or stale partials could previously end as isolated artifacts.
chains.hypothesis: Redacted harness summaries or loop-owned stale-partial evidence can be transformed into closed-loop candidate records.
chains.decision: Harness failures and stale partial readiness evidence are promoted into closed-loop candidate artifacts by either the harnesspromotion sidecar or a loop-owned candidate producer; candidates still require claim binding, verifier, CI gate, redacted evidence, decision record, and evidence graph edge before adoption.

chains.observation: Redacted live workflow summaries could be reused after or exactly at their evidence expiry boundary, allowing stale harness output to create fresh closed-loop candidates.
chains.hypothesis: Stamping generated_at and expires_at in the redacted summary, then requiring generated_at < expires_at and now < expires_at in harness promotion, prevents stale observations from entering the closed-loop backlog.
chains.decision: Harness promotion now treats evidence freshness as a strict merge gate: malformed windows, zero-length windows, expired summaries, and exact-expiry summaries cannot produce closed-loop candidate evidence.

chains.observation: The provider acceptance harness declared codex_provider_qa, openclaw_provider_qa, and daemon_runtime_snapshot observations, but the redacted smoke summary or loop manifest could omit structured provider coverage while still reporting generic contract coverage.
chains.hypothesis: Binding those observations to workflow source phrases, summary claims, machine-readable provider coverage, and the ai_thread_history loop identity lets agents see which provider/runtime paths and live v3 thread-history API surfaces were verified without reading raw live output or exporting secrets.
chains.decision: Provider acceptance evidence now exposes codex, OpenClaw, daemon runtime snapshot, and live v3 thread-history smoke coverage in the safe redacted summary path, while loop-registry evidence exposes codex/openclaw provider coverage and rejects observation/provider drift before merge; the same scheduled smoke artifact is also owned by ai_thread_history so product thread regressions are visible as loop evidence instead of only provider QA evidence.

chains.observation: Claim semantic hashes can become self-referential if semantic_hash metadata values inside bound generated files are treated as semantic input.
chains.hypothesis: Normalizing semantic_hash metadata values before hashing preserves real statement, policy, verifier, and bound-file meaning changes while preventing evidence refresh metadata from becoming its own meaning change.
chains.decision: Semantic hash metadata is now hash-inert evidence metadata; claim hashes still move when semantic content or bound executable surfaces move.

chains.observation: The AI Agent load harness produced useful stress evidence, but failures could remain a standalone load artifact instead of becoming a closed-loop adoption candidate.
chains.hypothesis: Scheduling the load harness and routing its redacted live summary through harness promotion lets performance or reliability failures enter the same candidate intake path as smoke failures.
chains.decision: Load/stress failures now have the same closed-loop promotion path as smoke failures: daily evidence refresh, redacted summary, candidate artifact, intake, and decision records.

chains.observation: A harness workflow can run harnesspromotion in the happy path but skip promotion or candidate artifact upload after the smoke/load step fails, and a newly registered harness loop can be omitted from the harness-promotion source manifest entirely.
chains.hypothesis: Verifying that both the harnesspromotion step and closed-loop candidate artifact upload step run under if: always(), and that every registered harness loop has exactly one promotion source with the same refresh workflow, keeps failed harness runs from becoming silent artifacts.
chains.decision: Harness promotion is now verified as a failure-path behavior and a source-coverage contract: registered harness failures must still produce closed-loop candidate evidence, and new harness loops cannot skip harness-promotion source coverage.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidates named required artifact types, but the candidate artifact did not itself carry executable commands for producing or verifying those artifacts; later producer-source growth also showed adoption plans can become passive if intake and decision loops do not consume every producer source, intake evidence did not expose adoption commands without reopening the candidate artifact, producer workflow changes could avoid the intake or decision verifier path, and loop refresh ignored-command candidates needed a subject-level next_artifact to avoid falling back to generic claim work.
chains.hypothesis: Embedding an adoption_plan in each candidate, exposing candidate_adoption_plans and producer-emitted candidate_subjects in intake evidence, allowing subject-bound candidates to name their intended next_artifact, verifying producer-source coverage in intake plus decision seed coverage, and binding each source workflow to intake/decision path triggers lets agents act from evidence artifacts even if they do not read the surrounding documentation.
chains.decision: Candidate artifacts now carry an adoption_plan, intake evidence exposes candidate_adoption_plans, candidate intake and decision evidence preserve producer-emitted candidate_subjects beside adoption and decision metadata, loop refresh ignored-command subjects pin verifier as their machine-routable next artifact, intake must cover every closed_loop_candidate producer source, decision verification requires an owned seed for every intake source, and producer workflow changes must trigger intake plus decision verification while still rejecting candidates whose plan does not cover every required next artifact.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidate artifacts required an evidence_graph_edge follow-up, but the candidate record did not name the concrete harness-to-closed-loop edge it was created from.
chains.hypothesis: Embedding promotion_edge in candidates, exposing promotion_edges and promotion_result in harness promotion evidence plus intake and decision evidence, and binding the claim to harness-failure observation plus verifier and CI coverage lets agents follow the failure-to-closed-loop path without reading narrative docs or opening the candidate artifact first.
chains.decision: Candidate artifacts now carry promotion_edge, harness promotion evidence carries the deduplicated promotion_edges list plus promotion_result for concrete summary promotions, intake consumes smoke/load/performance producer sources, decision verification rejects drift between the candidate edge and its source harness target, and loop closure audit regression keeps the promotion-edge claim from returning as an unbound coverage gap.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidate artifacts exposed source freshness at the artifact envelope, but an individual candidate item could be copied without its source workflow, run, expiry context, or claim-coverage dimensions.
chains.hypothesis: Embedding source_ref in each candidate, exposing candidate_source_refs in intake and decision evidence, verifying source_ref drift, and binding the source_ref claim to observe/verify/fail coverage keeps harness evidence context attached even when agents consume candidate items without reading surrounding docs.
chains.decision: Candidate artifacts now carry per-candidate source_ref, intake and decision evidence expose candidate_source_refs for every consumed producer source, verification rejects source_ref drift or missing source run identity, and loop closure audit regression keeps the source-ref claim from returning as an unbound coverage gap.

chains.observation: Harness failure candidates had source_ref and adoption_plan, but the candidate item still required agents to parse observation or hypothesis prose to know which harness failure claim it represented.
chains.hypothesis: Embedding a redacted machine-routable subject in harness-promoted candidates, then preserving candidate_subjects through intake, decision, and decision refresh command evidence lets follow-up agents route harness failures without reopening raw harness summaries or interpreting prose.
chains.decision: Harness-promoted closed-loop candidates now carry a redacted harness_failure subject, intake and decision evidence preserve that subject, and decision refresh command evidence exposes subject_kind so follow-up agents can route the failure without parsing observation or hypothesis prose.

chains.observation: Added business claims, changed claims, generated-doc bindings, or removed claims could change without bound code or tests changing in the same pull request.
chains.hypothesis: Comparing the PR diff against the loop registry can force claim additions, claim meaning changes, generated-doc binding changes, and claim removals to co-change bound code or test paths, not just manifests or generated docs.
chains.decision: PR impact verification rejects claim additions, claim meaning changes, generated-doc binding changes, and claim removals when the diff only changes manifests or generated docs; at least one bound code or test path must move, and the claim coverage tokens now make that enforcement visible to the loop-closure audit.

chains.observation: A business claim meaning change could co-change bound code or tests while leaving generated claim evidence or the evidence graph reasoning chain stale.
chains.hypothesis: Requiring generated claim evidence and the evidence graph reasoning manifest to change with claim meaning changes keeps human-readable generated surfaces, Observation, Hypothesis, Decision, and Next Loop aligned with the changed claim.
chains.decision: Claim meaning impact now requires generated claim evidence and reasoning evidence movement, preventing code/test-only claim edits from bypassing generated docs or the evidence graph, and its claim coverage tokens make that generated-evidence and reasoning-chain requirement visible to the loop-closure audit.

chains.observation: A claim-bound code or test path could change with only manifest evidence, or with generated-doc evidence while leaving the evidence graph reasoning chain stale.
chains.hypothesis: Requiring generated-doc evidence and evidence graph reasoning movement for claim-bound executable surface changes keeps human-readable generated surfaces, Observation, Hypothesis, Decision, and Next Loop aligned even when the claim statement itself does not change.
chains.decision: Bound executable surface changes now require reasoning evidence movement in addition to claim evidence, preventing code/test-only drift from bypassing the evidence graph.

chains.observation: Loop registry impact evidence exposed changed_file_count without the actual changed repository paths, and co-change failures returned an error before writing a machine-readable repair record, forcing agents and reviewers to rerun git diff or infer missing bound files, generated docs, and reasoning evidence from prose.
chains.hypothesis: Publishing a sorted changed_files list plus failed co-change violation records in impact evidence makes PR impact failure output self-contained and lets downstream agents infer semantic scope and repair actions from evidence alone.
chains.decision: Impact evidence now includes changed_files alongside changed_file_count and failed co-change violations with required bound files, generated evidence, reasoning evidence, and observed changed surfaces, so PR impact scope and repair actions are executable evidence rather than implicit git-diff or prose side channels.

chains.observation: The loop registry could reject semantic drift internally while its evidence artifact did not show each claim's code, test, manifest, generated doc, verifier, target command, and evidence-chain surface to downstream agents.
chains.hypothesis: Publishing per-claim surface evidence with target verifier commands and evidence graph chain ids, then rejecting manifest-only claims without code or test paths, lets agents infer the required co-change, QA, and reasoning scope from machine evidence instead of relying on narrative docs or memory.
chains.decision: Claim surface binding, target verifier commands, and evidence graph chain ids are now visible in loop-registry evidence and generated docs, and manifest-only claims are rejected so AI agents can detect executable code/test, QA, and reasoning scope from verifier output even when they skip prose.

chains.observation: Loop manifests declared verifies labels, but those labels could remain prose-like tokens that were not mapped to a concrete claim, verifier surface, or machine-readable failure condition.
chains.hypothesis: Adding covers_verifies, covers_observes, and covers_fails_when to claim bindings, then rejecting uncovered or unknown tokens, lets the loop registry derive QA scope and regression semantics from the manifest instead of relying on a human to interpret loop labels.
chains.decision: Loop verifies tokens are now executable coverage requirements: every token must be claimed by a business claim in the same loop, claim surfaces expose which verifies tokens they close, and loop-closure audit keeps the verifies coverage claim from returning as a claim-coverage candidate.

chains.observation: Loop coverage verification for observes, verifies, fails_when, and evidence used separate per-dimension algorithms, and the resulting coverage axes were not exposed as first-class evidence, so a future coverage axis or behavior change required agents to remember multiple files instead of reading one executable semantic table.
chains.hypothesis: A static loop coverage dimension registry can bind each axis to loop token extraction, claim token extraction, completion checking, top-level verification dispatch, evidence JSON, and generated docs, while registry and evidence tests prove every axis has executable handlers and a machine-readable surface.
chains.decision: Loop coverage dimensions now share one executable registry; observes, verifies, fails_when, and evidence coverage still keep their public verifier wrappers, but behavior changes must co-change through the registry, evidence JSON, generated docs, and registry/evidence tests instead of scattered per-axis implementations.

chains.observation: Loop manifests declared observes labels, but those labels could remain prose-like tokens that were not mapped to a concrete claim, evidence surface, or machine-readable failure condition.

chains.decision: Loop observes tokens are now executable coverage requirements: every token must be claimed by a business claim in the same loop, claim surfaces expose which observes tokens they close, and loop-closure audit keeps the observation coverage claim from returning as a claim-coverage candidate.

chains.hypothesis: Adding covers_fails_when to claim bindings, rejecting uncovered or unknown tokens, and binding the rule to regression_pattern observations lets the loop registry derive failure semantics from the manifest instead of relying on a human to interpret loop labels.
chains.decision: Loop fails_when tokens are now executable coverage requirements: every token must be claimed by a business claim in the same loop, claim surfaces expose which failure conditions they close, and loopclosureaudit keeps the rule bound to explicit regression and claim-without-verifier failure tokens.

chains.observation: Loop manifests declared evidence source paths, but those paths could remain artifact labels that were not mapped to a concrete claim and evidence surface, or the claim could lack observe/fail tokens that tell agents this is an evidence-expiry and regression-pattern rule.
chains.hypothesis: Adding covers_evidence to claim bindings, rejecting uncovered or unknown evidence paths, and binding the claim to evidence_expired/regression_pattern observations lets the loop registry derive artifact-to-claim meaning from the manifest instead of relying on a human to interpret artifact names.
chains.decision: Loop evidence source paths are now executable coverage requirements: every path must be claimed by a business claim in the same loop, claim surfaces expose which evidence artifacts they close, and loopclosureaudit keeps the rule bound to explicit evidence-expiry observe/fail tokens.

chains.observation: Loop evidence sources had machine-readable paths, but their kind field could drift into free-form values before product QA evidence such as API snapshots or screenshots became first-class evidence modalities.

chains.decision: Loop registry evidence now carries graph edges, rejects both harness promotes_to targets without matching promotion edges and claim bindings without loop-owned enforces edges, and loop-closure audit keeps the graph-edge claim bound to harness failure and claim coverage failure semantics.

chains.hypothesis: Emitting GitHub Actions annotations from the evidence graph impact surface makes changed files, changed evidence chain ids, executable refs, claim ids, and next-loop targets visible in the PR check output, so agents can repair the executable reasoning graph without reading narrative docs first.

chains.observation: Harness-like workflow names could be added without being registered as harness loops, explicitly excluded from harness ownership, or bound to observe/verify/fail tokens that tell agents this is a harness-failure promotion rule; reason-only exclusions still forced humans to infer which executable surface replaced the harness loop.
chains.hypothesis: Scanning smoke, load, and harness workflow filenames, requiring either a harness loop registration or an exclusion with replacement claim and replacement evidence, and binding the claim to harness_failure/regression_pattern observations keeps new QA workflows bound to closed-loop promotion semantics without relying on prose interpretation.

chains.observation: The generated endpoint smoke matrix workflow looked harness-like by filename, but it is intended to be a contract and generator gate; without a replacement claim/evidence binding, agents had to trust prose to know why it was excluded from harness failure promotion.
chains.hypothesis: Binding the workflow to a dedicated contract-gate claim, smoke matrix manifest, generated doc, OpenAPI parity tests, generated endpoint smoke tests, and uploaded evidence artifact makes the exclusion executable and keeps future workflow changes from silently becoming unpromoted QA harnesses.
chains.decision: Generated endpoint smoke matrix remains excluded from harness promotion only as long as its contract/generator claim, tests, generated docs, workflow, and evidence artifact stay connected; candidate-decision review expiry or dynamic harness-failure template changes may update shared loop-registry and candidate-decision surfaces, but they do not reclassify this workflow as a failure-promoting harness unless the smoke-matrix workflow, manifest, tests, or evidence artifact change. Live testnet smoke failures now route redacted dynamic claim ids through the harness_failure decision template while keeping a smoke source_coverage_seed, which restores main decision verification without changing generated endpoint smoke matrix workflow, manifest, tests, docs, or uploaded evidence artifact semantics. Local pressure follow-up and metrics snapshot evidence may update operational-readiness artifacts and the shared loop-registry hash surface, but they change only capacity/latency/allocation evidence and do not alter the generated endpoint smoke matrix workflow, manifest, tests, docs, or uploaded evidence artifact semantics.

chains.observation: The existing device daemon client API exposed only the preferred daemon for a device, so clients could not render multiple profile-specific daemon instances such as staging, development, and production without inferring hidden server state.
chains.hypothesis: Adding a read-only plural device daemon endpoint, binding it to the route classifier, store query, HTTP test, generated endpoint smoke matrix, and loop-registry evidence surface lets the client inspect daemon instances without changing the existing preferred daemon compatibility endpoint.
chains.decision: GET /devices/{device_id}/daemon remains the single preferred daemon compatibility endpoint, while GET /devices/{device_id}/daemons is a read-only plural projection sorted newest first and filtered through the same device and daemon visibility checks; route and HTTP tests prove the new surface is explicit instead of inferred by clients. Redacted live probes now prove the plural v1/v2 routes are present and auth-protected, not 404, across staging, development, and production after deployment. The latest Notion QA comment-event diff keeps the frontend handoff comment id executable, so stale page-level Notion readback cannot reopen the server API without a fresh route or contract failure.

chains.decision: Container image contract ownership is now routed through executable evidence: containercontract validation and verification helpers are split below the 75-line budget, required fields are a static registry, tools/containercontract has a zero-over-budget ratchet, and changed-path impact evidence can select container contract verifiers from the loop registry instead of agent memory.

chains.observation: Control-plane performance, high-traffic audit, and loop-closure audit evidence were machine-readable but lacked generated_at/expires_at windows, so refresh automation could not distinguish fresh open-loop measurements from stale proof artifacts.
chains.hypothesis: Giving these meta-evidence sidecars the same 24h evidence window as core loop evidence lets refresh dispatch and downstream agents reject stale performance, audit, and closure evidence without embedding dynamic timestamps in generated prose.
chains.decision: Performance, high-traffic audit, and loop-closure audit evidence now carry generated_at/expires_at in JSON evidence only; generated docs remain deterministic while refresh automation can expire stale proof artifacts after 24h.

chains.observation: The control-plane HTTP server entrypoint had accumulated AI Agent client routes, daemon routes, component-task routes, SSE streaming, and progress ingestion in one 1107-line file, and its top-level route registration was still a hand-written HandleFunc list, forcing agents to load unrelated concepts before changing a single endpoint surface.
chains.hypothesis: A mechanical semantic split plus a verified static route registry can preserve every endpoint and handler body while lowering inference cost: each route family gets its own file, progress ingestion gets request/event/response helpers, route patterns become data, and module-decomposition ratchets make the reduction observable.
chains.decision: The server route surface is now represented as bounded semantic handler files and a verified static route registry instead of one monolithic server.go and hand-written mux registration; the split files are claim-bound, workflow-triggered, and covered by module-decomposition evidence so future route work cannot bypass the same verifier surface.

chains.observation: The Notion QA completion-progress P0 still needed evidence that a completed AI Agent assignment cannot be made to look active again by late daemon progress. Existing stop-terminal tests covered user stop, but completed terminal state had no HTTP-level v2/v3/subscription/SSE replay proof. Updating operational-readiness also changed loop-registry generated surfaces that are claim-bound to generated endpoint and route-handler gates.
chains.hypothesis: A focused HTTP regression test can prove the completed terminal path without changing endpoints: after assignment poll, running log, and assignment_completed, a late /thread-progress batch for the same assignment/thread/run must be rejected and must not leak into v2 threads, v3 history, active_thread_filters, or SSE replay. Binding that proof into operational-readiness and evidence-graph keeps generated endpoint and route-handler claims honest while leaving the product P0 partial until a same-moment browser/network reproduction is captured.
chains.decision: The server side of the completed-but-still-progressing P0 is now narrower: completed assignments reject late daemon progress and expose no active stream/filter/replay residue across v2 and v3 HTTP surfaces. This is not product closure; operational-readiness stays partial until the next actual UI recurrence is captured with the redacted same-conversation v3/v2/subscription/SSE tool plus screenshot.

chains.observation: Loop Registry semantic hashes bind code to SSOT value claims, but Go syntax pattern coverage and relocation evidence are not yet machine-routable for metaprogramming refactors.
chains.hypothesis: A JSON-driven syntax hash graph can expand through behavior-golden packages, derive deterministic AST-normalized file and package hashes, and connect them to the existing semantic hash without changing runtime behavior.
chains.decision: Adopt the syntax hash graph as a staged golden-first spike: contextmap, awsadapters, cmd/riido_ai_server runtime config, internal/repoidentity, internal/contractscompat, tools/requestauth, tools/healthreadycmd, tools/runtimeboundary, tools/configreference, tools/storesaferouting, tools/publicpageslive, tools/gocibaseline, tools/webfrontendapi, tools/aiagentrisk, and the syntaxhash tool are golden-locked before analysis, semantic hash generation remains the existing Loop Registry implementation, and syntax hash evidence records target coverage, repository coverage, collision-free hashes, relocation mappings, score, and generated artifact physical constraints.

loop.observation: Evidence artifacts existed, but the reasoning chain from observation to next loop was still scattered across generated readers and PR memory.
loop.hypothesis: A compact evidence graph can make the development loop navigable by tools without asking an AI to read every narrative document.
loop.execute: Verify every chain has observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next-loop nodes; verify repository refs exist; generate this reader and publish graph evidence in CI.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails on incomplete chains, duplicate ids, missing refs, stale generated docs, missing strict workflow evidence, or missing redaction on artifact evidence.
loop.retrospective: This makes the evidence loop itself inspectable: future agents can see why a loop exists, what changed, what verifies it, and what loop should run next.
